quests.title: The Quiet Carriage, Lewisham
quests.blurb: Nobody else has offered, so. The quiet carriage runs on shame and somebody on the the second express out of Lewisham has stopped feeling it. It started small, the way these things do. Ride it, see the crime, and apply the shame manually. Just do not come back empty-handed.

steps.label: ride the quiet carriage and observe the crime
apply the shame manually
photograph the sign, for the record

quests.title: The Jannali Shortcut
quests.blurb: I'll be straight with you. Every courier has a route that is not on a map and mine goes through Jannali. Everyone I have told has looked at me the way you are now. They have started locking one end. Go and find out whether it is locked forever or just locked today. I'll see you right for it.

steps.label: the end they lock
the long way round, so you understand what it costs
$54, which is what the long way costs me a week

quests.title: Possession at Carlton
quests.blurb: It is not a police matter and I have checked. Third time at Carlton on a Tuesday. I have got a photo on my phone but it is useless. Not kids — kids run. This one walks, and I have stopped filling in the form. I need it stopped before somebody writes a very long report about me. I'll put the kettle on for when you're back.

steps.label: where they come through the fence
the ones who think a hard hat is a costume
photograph the gap so I can put a number on the form

quests.title: The Exhibition Centre Regular
quests.blurb: Right. Since you asked. A man drank in my front bar by Exhibition Centre for 13 years and then stopped, and every regular in here has gone vague on me at once, which means they know. It might be nothing. It has not felt like nothing. You are not from here. Go and knock. I will know if you skipped a bit.

steps.label: the house they say he moved to
you cannot ask a favour empty-handed
come back and tell me straight

quests.title: Bay 14, Penrith
quests.blurb: There is no clever way to say this. Two hundred bays at Penrith and I have counted two hundred and forty cars in here on the week of the show. The paperwork says one thing and my eyes say another. One of them has not moved since March and it has a ticket on it from March. I'll see you right for it.

steps.label: the car, and the ticket, and the date on it
the two arguing over the grass
$52 in fines nobody is going to collect

quests.title: Whatever Is Under the Grey at Cowan
quests.blurb: It is the sort of thing you notice or you do not. One colour, grey, the same grey in Cowan as in every other suburb. It started small, the way these things do. I would like something of this one to exist afterwards, and I am the only one who seems to have noticed. I will know if you skipped a bit.

steps.label: the wall, before they get to it
photograph it properly, not a phone-in-a-hurry job
show me

quests.title: The Hill Above Central Chalmers Street
quests.blurb: Do not laugh. There is a bench on the hill above Central Chalmers Street I have watched from a moving bus about fourteen thousand times. This is the third time I have had this conversation. I am not going to stop — that is not the kind of person I turned out to be. So you go, at knock-off, when the light is worth it. Just do not come back empty-handed.

steps.label: up the hill, the way the road does not go
the view I have never stopped for
$72, because I am paying you for it

quests.title: Contesting It at Tramway Avenue
quests.blurb: Do not laugh. Done at Tramway Avenue on grand final week for something that is only an offence if a sign says so, and nobody upstairs wants to hear it. This is the third time I have had this conversation. How do you photograph a thing not being somewhere? That is your problem now. Just do not come back empty-handed.

steps.label: where the sign is supposed to be
photograph the absence, which is harder than it sounds
the one who tells you photography is not allowed here

quests.title: The Strip Outside Central
quests.blurb: Two people have already said no. Nobody planted the strip at Central. It is the not knowing that has got me, honestly. I did, on school holidays, at quarter to six, so nobody would ask. I would like the fifteenth to go badly for council. Say nothing to anyone on the way.

steps.label: the strip, which is a garden now
the man with the whipper snipper
photograph it while it still exists

quests.title: Night Fill, Westmead Hospital
quests.blurb: It is the sort of thing you notice or you do not. Started on grand final week. It started small, the way these things do. In off the Westmead Hospital late train, gone before the first delivery, every time, and I am past being reasonable about it. Come in on the late one and watch the loading door. I will know if you skipped a bit.

steps.label: come in on the late one like they do
the loading door nobody watches
whoever is standing in it at two in the morning
